instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`).

Problem: a thick-walled cylinder with inner radius 10 mm and outer radius 20 mm is loaded by an internal pressure of 50 MPa. Model a plane-strain slice: axisymmetric CAX4 elements in the x-y plane at z = 0 (CalculiX requires 2D elements in the z=0 plane), with the radial coordinate x in [10, 20] mm, the axial coordinate y in [0, 1] mm, and the axial displacement u_y = 0 on every node (so the axial strain is zero).

Build the mesh and the deck `/home/user/Desktop/solution.inp`:
- 21 radial stations at `x = 10 + 0.5*i` for i = 0..20, each duplicated at y = 0 and y = 1 (42 nodes total; node ids and ordering are yours)
- 20 CAX4 elements, one per radial interval; element node ordering must be a valid counter-clockwise quad in the x-y plane
- material: E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3, one `*Solid Section` covering every element
- boundary: u_y = 0 (dof 2) on every node; do not constrain the radial displacement
- load: 50 MPa internal pressure on the inner surface (in CalculiX, the CAX4 face P4 is the inner radial face for the counter-clockwise ordering above); apply it only to the element touching r = 10, not to every radial layer
- step: `*Static`

CalculiX allows at most 16 entries per data line; split long `*Nset`/`*Elset` lists across multiple lines. Results reach `.dat` through `*Node Print` (which needs an explicit node set).

Submit the job with `/usr/bin/ccx` and produce `/home/user/Desktop/solution.dat`.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as two comma-separated numbers: `ur_inner, ur_outer` where
- `ur_inner` is the radial displacement (mm) at the inner surface r = 10 (any z, it is constant),
- `ur_outer` is the radial displacement (mm) at the outer surface r = 20.

The evaluator re-solves your deck independently; the reported numbers must come from your own run.
